## П17. Заметка docs/notes/a2-attn-bwd.md

# A2: the attention backward as batched GEMMs (branch claude/e1-exit-attn)

Recommendation of external review 2 (`docs/briefs/astra-answer-2-2026-10-31.md`, section 2): replace
`aten::_efficient_attention_backward` (fmha_cutlassB sm_75, ~0.8 ms per layer at 4 rows of ~200
tokens on the T4) by cuBLAS batched GEMMs and own Triton kernels for the softmax parts.

## What is in the branch

`solution/attn_bwd.py`, switch `SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_BWD=math` (default `sdpa` = the original
backward, nothing changes). Wiring: `solution/unpad.py`, three lines in `_VarlenAttention`
(the forward records the step's `Plan`, the backward asks `attn_bwd.backward` first) and one line in
`patch_qwen2_attention` (warm-up and exit log, math mode only). The forward, the attention recompute
of `fused_proj.py` and `_AttnBlock` (SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_ONE_FUNCTION, off by default) are untouched.

Per layer: one gather kernel (q, grad_out, k, v token-major -> head-major padded bins), per chunk of
(bin, kv group) entries and per block of query rows five strided-batched GEMMs (S = QK^T fp32 out via
`bmm(out_dtype=float32)`, dV += P^T dO fp32, dP = dO V^T fp32 out, dQ = dS K, dK += dS^T Q fp32) and
two row kernels (causal softmax over each row's own sequence -> P fp16; dS = scale P (dP - sum P dP)
over P), one scatter kernel back to token-major (dK, dV rounded to half once) with zeros for the
alignment tail. GQA: the six query heads of a kv group are consecutive rows of the head-major buffer,
so dK and dV sum them inside the GEMM (no expansion copies, no group sums). Sequences are packed
into bins of LP rows (`layout`: longest row rounded up to NB blocks of 16-multiples, first fit,
longest first): short rows share one square. Query rows go in NB blocks per bin
(SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_BWD_BLOCKS, default 2): block t only meets keys 0 .. (t+1) LP / NB - 1, so the
products skip the causal square's upper right part (NB = 2: 3/4 of the square, NB = 4: 5/8). S and
P live in the free tail of fused_proj's shared dequantization buffer (15.75 MiB behind the q|k|v|o
weights the o_proj and q/k/v backward read), as many entries per chunk as fit.
Filter, decided once per step from the row lengths: at least SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_BWD_MIN_TOKENS real
tokens (600), the longest row at most SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_BWD_MAX_LEN (256), and `work_ratio` (the
math path's score entries over the fmha's causal ones) at most SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_BWD_MAX_RATIO;
anything unexpected or an error -> the original backward.

Own kernels: attn_bwd_gather_kernel, attn_bwd_probs_kernel, attn_bwd_dscores_kernel,
attn_bwd_scatter_kernel (check_rules likeness to the example 0.31 / 0.31 / 0.69 / 0.24).

## Numerics

Not bitwise (the brief allows it). Against an fp32 autograd reference (max |err| / max |ref|), random
fp16 q/k/v/dO, 4 rows (T4, below): the original path 2.9e-4 .. 7.9e-4, the math path (NB = 2) 2.5e-4 ..
6.2e-4 (same order,
slightly better: delta from P and dP in fp32 instead of dO . O with O rounded). Tail rows exactly zero.

## Tests (`solution/test_attn_bwd.py`, laptop)

Gradients against the fp32 reference and the original path for four length patterns with and
without the tail (bins 4/3/2/1), the scratch in the shared buffer (held weights untouched, the same
bits as allocated scratch, chunks of 3/3/2 within 1e-3), the allocation cap, the wiring through
`unpad.attention` inside `varlen` (forward bitwise unchanged, one math call; outside the filter the
original backward, dk/dv bitwise), no math call outside `varlen` or with the switch off, guards,
warm-up compile. `test_unpad.py` 30/30 with the hook in place.

## T4: no-go

`solution/bench_attn_bwd.py`, T4 (peagverr, soup-e1-a2b4, f944614, 30 timed calls per entry, medians
of CUDA-event times; one layer's backward alone: q, k, v, grad_out and the forward's out/lse given,
so the attention recompute, which both paths run the same way, is not in the numbers). orig: unpad's
path (k/v expansion, fmha backward, group sums); nb = 1/2/4: the math path with that many query-row
blocks; r2: work_ratio at NB = 2; host: ms of CPU to queue one call (GPU idle); MiB: peak allocated
above the inputs (math: scratch allocated, at most 16 MiB; in training it sits in the shared buffer).

Also measured: the scores GEMM at L = 208 (8 batches of 1248 x 208 x 128) takes 0.082 ms with
`bmm(out_dtype=float32)`, 0.126 ms as a half bmm plus a cast, 0.064 ms as a half bmm alone (so
out_dtype works on sm_75 and is the cheaper way to fp32 scores); the row kernels' warps (1/2/4/8) move
the whole call by under 10 % (2 kept).

Verdict (the brief's rule: stop unless < 0.5 ms per layer at L ~ 208): **no-go, A2 closed.** The best
math variant at 4 x ~200 tokens is 0.78 ms against 0.84; the original is faster on every batch shaped
like the task's data (one long row and shorter ones: 0.45-0.68 ms against 0.70-1.30) and on every even
batch from L = 320 up. The only wins are near-even batches of 4 x 200-256 tokens (-0.06 and -0.22 ms
per layer), which random batches of this data almost never form (2-4 of 64 steps have even a
longest row <= 256 at >= 600 tokens). Why: on the power-limited T4 these strided-batched GEMMs run at
5-7 TFLOPS and cost 0.06-0.08 ms each however small, so five GEMMs per row block plus the four own
launches put a floor of ~0.7 ms under the math path, while the fmha kernel skips the causal half and
all padding (its time follows the sum of L^2 / 2: 0.45 ms at the data's typical batch). Queueing costs
0.6-1.6 ms of CPU per layer against 0.18 (16-44 launches), which would also eat the GPU lag of the
long steps. Nothing here makes the 0.5 ms target reachable without an own tensor-core kernel (review
2, section 2.5: not the plan for today).

The code stays in the branch, off by default (`SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_BWD=sdpa`): with the default, the
forward's `taken` and the backward's hook return on their first comparison. Recommendation: do not
merge the `unpad.py` hook and `attn_bwd.py` into main (no gain, more for the jury to read); this note
and the bench numbers are the result. No full run with ATTN_BWD=math was made (the brief asked for it
only after a passing microbench).

## Fallback items after the no-go

(i) Labelled-only backward of the final norm and the last MLP (review 1, last block): not taken. The
last layer's MLP has no LoRA, so its backward is three input-gradient GEMMs plus SwiGLU (~3.2 ms per
step at 830 tokens); rows whose head gradient is zero give zero there, so gathering the labelled rows
would save (1 - labelled share) of that, ~0.1 s per run at best, below one session's noise, and it
needs a gather/scatter through fused_proj's `_MLP`, the offload of gate|up and int8_bwd (C1's files
today). Not worth the risk on the last day.

(ii) `SOUP_SOLUTION_NORM_HALF=1` (review 2, section 4.2; R3's row "float16_copy"), in the branch, off,
not measured on the T4: the orchestrator stopped both fallback items before the ABBA (fused_proj.py
and rmsnorm.py belong to C1 today) and moved me to the save tail (`docs/notes/save-tail.md`). The decoder
layer's input norm and post-attention norm write their output's half copy in the same kernel
(`rmsnorm.rms_norm_rows_fwd_half`), attached to the fp32 output; `_QKVRope` and `_MLP` take it through
`rmsnorm.half_of` instead of `x.to(half)` (fused_proj.py: two lines and the import). The final norm
does not write one (the head gathers and casts its own rows). Bitwise: the copy is the cast's value
(round to nearest even of the same fp32 product), and the new kernel keeps rms_norm_rows_fwd's tile
layout: left to itself Triton gives the half store 8-wide vectors, the tile becomes sizePerThread
[1, 8] instead of [1, 4] and the sum of squares is added in another order (rstd and y then differ in
the last bit); with stride_y16 not specialized the half store stays narrow and rstd/y are the
original kernel's bits (tested: plain and fused-add norms; a tiny 4-bit Qwen2 with LoRA through the
fused path gives equal hidden states, loss and every LoRA gradient with the switch on and off).
`half_of` hands the copy over once (the fp32 output lets go of it, so it lives as long as the
consumer keeps it, as the cast did) and falls back to the cast when the output changed since the
norm (version check), the dtype or shape differs, or no copy exists; `_MLP` keeps its single padded
copy when there is none. Note: test_recompute's decoder-layer memory test fails when it runs after
any tiny-model test in the same process, on main too (order dependence, not this change).
Laptop (RTX 3050 Ti, per norm at 830 / 1,440 rows): norm + cast 157 / 230 us (plain), 199 / 320 us
(with the add) against 110 / 169 and 165 / 250 us: -35..-70 us per norm, 56 norms per step, plus 56
cast launches less. Warm-up: `rms_norm_rows_fwd_half` registered by `patch_qwen2_rmsnorm` (two
classes, as rms_norm_rows_fwd).

NORM_HALF on the T4: the orchestrator allowed the ABBA after all (31 Oct ~12:40); it runs in the same
session as the save tail (`soup-e1-tail1`, account 3, commit e4b9f3c, variant `half:`; see
`docs/notes/save-tail.md` for how to fetch it). Merge rule: >= 0.1 s in that session, peak unchanged
(371 MiB), bitwise (tested locally). To turn it on: `os.environ.setdefault("SOUP_SOLUTION_NORM_HALF", "1")`
in `apply()`; its two consumer lines in fused_proj.py may conflict with C1's edits (only those lines).

NORM_HALF in soup-e1-tail1 (variant `half`, positions 3 and 4 of the ABBA): steps 3+ 25.83 / 26.28 s
against base 23.44 / 26.87 and once (no step change at all) 24.63 / 27.18: the session's drift
(+3.4 s from the first to the last base run, concave) is 10-30x the expected effect, so the wall says
nothing; peak 371 MiB, reserved 250, allocated 225.5 as base; rms_norm_rows_fwd_half launched in both
half runs (check 3).

Per-norm cost on the T4 (`solution.bench_norm_half 300`, peagverr soup-e1-nhb1, d79ad23; medians of
300 CUDA-event timings; every call bitwise: y, rstd and the half copy equal to rms_norm_rows_fwd plus
the cast):

| tokens | plain: norm + cast / half-writing norm, us | fused add: norm + cast / half-writing, us | per step (1 plain + 55 add), ms |
|---:|---|---|---:|
| 400 | 77.8 / 65.5 | 90.1 / 84.0 | 0.35 |
| 600 | 92.1 / 79.7 | 122.7 / 106.7 | 0.90 |
| 830 | 115.2 / 93.8 | 149.9 / 129.2 | 1.16 |
| 1,100 | 142.3 / 113.9 | 188.4 / 158.7 | 1.66 |

Over the 64 steps of the task's data (simulated batches, mean 826 tokens): 76 ms of GPU time per run,

Jury run (seed 57, rows 20000/35000): all 10 checks, 46.2 / 47.9 s against 88.3 s, 411 MiB,
eval +0.008 %.

Why night-boundary did nothing: every forward slices `layers[:n]`, which re-registers the layers,
and that dropped its cached lists every step.

Follow-ups: the embedding lookup's `.to("cpu")` (unpad/C1 files). Also warmup `step_ops` creates
tensors without a dtype: it races with the loader's fp16 default dtype and fails at times.

## Where the time went (T4 trace of main a6c3fe3, soup-b1-diag0, steps 8-9 under the profiler)

- Harness: `Probe.on_step_begin` and `on_step_end` call `torch.cuda.synchronize()` (harness/_train.py),
  so the queue is empty at both ends of every step; anything between `on_step_end` and the next
  `on_step_begin` (log, Soup callbacks, DataLoader) runs with the GPU idle whatever we do.
- Inside the step: the forward is GPU-bound (the head's `int(labelled.sum().item())` waited 69.6 ms
  for it), the head is PCIe-bound, the TRL metric `.item()` waited 33 ms for the head, the backward
  is GPU-bound in long steps (transformers' nan/inf check of the loss waited 62.9 ms for it) and
  CPU-bound in short ones. The in-step drains cost only ~2-4 ms of GPU idle (backward start).
- Boundary (end of backward 530.8 ms -> first layer kernel 562.0 ms): ~31 ms GPU idle: FLOP
  counter walk 4.9 ms, clip launches ~5 ms (Python over ~450 parameters), AdamW 2.8 ms (GPU 0.8),
  after Adam 3.2 ms, log + callbacks 4.6 ms, DataLoader fetch/collate 2.7 ms, step start 3.4 ms,
  forward start (pack_batch nonzero/tolist, embedding host gather, cu_seqlens copy) 2.7 ms.
- Why night-boundary measured nothing: (1) every forward slices `layers[:num_hidden_layers]`
  (unpad.varlen_model_forward and HF's Qwen2Model alike); a sliced ModuleList registers all 28
  layers into a new ModuleList, which fired torch's global registration hook and dropped the cached
  lists every step, so the FLOP counter rebuilt them (8.8 ms per call on the T4, timing run); (2)
  its `train()` fast path never engaged (Qwen2 models use `PreTrainedModel.train` in
  transformers 5.16, and its own `PeftModel.train` failed its "plain" check). Both fixed: only
  registrations on the listed model's own modules drop the lists; PreTrainedModel.train is accepted
  while `use_kernels` is off (checked per call).

## What changed (each behind a switch; all on by default after 1be9e55)

- `SOUP_SOLUTION_STEP_BOUNDARY` (boundary.py, from night-boundary, fixed as above): FLOP count, clip,
  zero_grad, train() from per-run lists.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_NAN_FILTER=gpu` (step_pipeline.py): transformers' nan/inf filter of the logged loss
  as `torch.where(isfinite(loss), loss, _tr_loss / k)` returned by training_step, the host check
  switched off for the epoch (restored after it and around checkpoint saves): the same addend bit for
  bit, no wait after the backward; the CPU queues the clip during the backward.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_PREFETCH_BATCH` (step_pipeline.py): the batch after next is fetched and collated
  right after the backward is queued (main thread, not a background thread or process), same batches
  in the same order, the rewind FIFO gets the same indices in the same order.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_HOST_PLAN` (step_pipeline.py, fused_ce.py, the labelled-count line of
  head_stream.py): the unpad plan, the head's labelled count and `num_items_in_batch` from the batch's
  CPU tensors where the DataLoader hands it over, one non-blocking pinned copy; matched to the GPU
  tensors by identity, anything else takes the GPU path.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_DEFER_METRICS` (trainer_patch.py): TRL metrics and Soup's rewind rows stay on the
  GPU until TRL's log(), read there in one device-to-host copy (float64 holds every fp32 value and
  count exactly); same floats in the same log entries, same rewind.jsonl lines.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_BWD_SINGLE_THREAD` (step_pipeline.py, from the external review): the trainer's
  `accelerator.backward` under `torch.autograd.set_multithreading_enabled(False)`: the backward runs
  on the calling thread, so one cuBLAS handle/workspace serves forward and backward (the autograd
  device thread made a second one). Bitwise the same step (test through the weight ring, the MLP
  offload's events and the attention recompute; the backward hooks run on the calling thread).
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_BOUNDARY_TIMING=1` (diagnostics only): host ms of every callback per event, the log,
  Soup's tracker and display, the boundary's own wrappers, list rebuilds.

## Step 1: what the CPU does per step (T4, main a6c3fe3 + profiler, session soup-c1-prof, 3ace6b7)

`SOUP_SOLUTION_CPU_PROFILE=1` (`solution/cpu_profile.py`, off by default, wired in `apply()` next to
the diag switch): per step tokens / wall / issue / main-thread and process CPU; cProfile of steps 5-8
(all threads: Python 3.13 profiles every thread); a 1 ms stack sampler over steps 9-12 (main thread
and autograd's device thread, where the backward's Python runs); the synchronizing CUDA calls of step
13 with their call sites; a CUDA-event timeline (where the GPU waits for the CPU) for the other steps.

Counts per step (cProfile, exact): 681 Triton launches of ours (each also pays the harness's two
timed events and two `torch.cuda.current_stream()` chains), 2,457 `Event.record`, 736 `wait_event`,
366 `torch.cuda.stream()` contexts, 2,406 `torch.cuda.current_stream()` calls (1,362 the harness's),
2,265 `Params4bit.__torch_function__` calls (~1,090 in our dequantizations and guards, the rest the
step boundary's walks over the model, task B1), 395 autograd Function round trips, 369 saved-tensor
packs and 503 unpacks, 230 `.item()` (AdamW's step counters, B1). GPU side (diag trace, steps 8-9):
2,090 kernel launches per step (681 Triton, ~1,270 torch, ~140 cuBLAS), 422 memcpy, 107 memset.
Launches by node: AddRMSNorm backward (the attention recompute runs inside it) 166 Triton + 84
copies, `_MLP` forward/backward 112 Triton each, `_QKVRope` backward 112 + 83 GEMMs, varlen
attention 56 head-expansion copies each way plus 56 group sums.

Host synchronizations of a step (sync debug mode, step 13: 22): Soup's rewind
`row_losses_from_token_losses` 8, TRL metrics in trainer_patch 4, transformers' nan check 2,

## Step 2: what changed (all bit-identical, each behind a switch, defaults on)

- `SOUP_SOLUTION_DEQUANT_REUSE=1` (fused_proj.py, under the CPU diet): q, k, v and o dequantized in
  one launch (`nf4_dequant4_kernel`, replaces dequant3 in the warm-up); the o_proj forward, the
  recompute's o_proj, the o_proj backward and the q/k/v backward read what the shared buffer holds
  (`_HELD`: every `_buffer()` call forgets it, so any other writer invalidates); any other repeat of
  what the buffer holds is skipped too (the last layer's down_proj into the backward). 4 Triton
  launches per layer less (681 -> 569 per step) and 3 dequantizations of GPU work. The kernel's
  operands kept per packed weight (`_nf4_args`, keyed by storage pointer and the ids of the quant
  state's tensors): no Params4bit attribute reads and no views per launch. Guards: imports cached,
  Params4bit getters read with the function override off, bitsandbytes' small-M verdict memoized.
  Dropout RNG state through the generator itself.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_FEWER_VIEWS=1` (fused_proj.py, rope.py): rope launched from strides
  (`rope._launch_strided`: the same kernel arguments as on the head-major views) and the recompute's
  q, k, v built in the attention kernel's token-major layout directly (same pointers, sizes and
  strides as `kernel_operands`); ~20 view ops less per layer and step. The transposes of the shared
  buffer's weight views and the adapter halves' views are made once (kept with the buffers); a
  layer's q/k/v/o operands are checked once per plan (8.2 -> 1.9 us per call on the laptop).
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_ONE_FUNCTION` (fused_proj.py, **off by default**): a recomputing layer's
  `_QKVRope`, varlen attention and o_proj as one autograd node (`_AttnBlock`), the same ops in the
  same order; tested bitwise, faster on short steps, but +4.2 MiB allocated peak (see ABBA 2).
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_MLP_ADDMM_INPLACE=1` (fused_proj.py): the MLP input gradient's second GEMM adds into
  the first's fp32 result in place (torch's out-of-place addmm copied it first): 28 D2D copies and
  one N x 1536 fp32 buffer per layer less.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_LAYER_EXIT_HOOK=1` (weight_stream.py): the layer's backward marker as a tensor hook
  instead of the `_LayerExit` identity node (autograd runs it at the same point).
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_FAST_STREAMS=1` (weight_stream.py, head_stream.py, offload.py): side streams
  selected by torch's C setter instead of `torch.cuda.stream()` (5.3 -> 0.3 us on the laptop), the
  current stream read as its id triple and its Stream object reused (1.8 -> 0.06 us), one reused
  event for the offloader's side-stream waits.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_STREAM_TIMING=0`: the attention group's and the head's copies and waits untimed (no
  timing events, no queries); `=1` gives the old log lines.
- head_stream.py: the chunk loop with pre-built slot, host and logits views.

one node vs three bitwise with dropout 0 and 0.05; in-place accumulate bitwise in both MLP modes),

### 2. Two nodes instead of one (`SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_TWO_NODES=1`, fused_proj.py, on by default)

Why one node cost +4.2 MiB: autograd holds a node's incoming gradient until the node returns, and
`_AttnBlock`'s incoming gradient is the o_proj output's (N x 1536 half), alive through the attention
backward, the layer's peak. `_QKVAttn` is `_QKVRope` + the variable-length attention as one node
(the reshape to the o_proj input a view of its output); the o_proj stays `_Linear4bitHalf`. Its
backward consumes the output's gradient first, as with three nodes; `_QKVAttn` then holds its own
incoming gradient (the attention output's, N x 1536 half) through the q/k/v backward, in place of the
q/k/v gradients (N x 2048 half) that `_QKVRope`'s node held there, and the q/k/v gradients die as soon
as they are in `g` (`_qkv_backward(box=...)` takes the only references). Same ops, operands and order
as `_AttnBlock`'s token-major path. `SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_ONE_FUNCTION=1` still wins when set; eval, the
non-recomputing layers and attention dropout take the three nodes.

Tests (`test_fused_proj.py`): `test_attention_two_nodes_is_bitwise` (three, two and one node: output,
input gradient and LoRA gradients bit for bit, LoRA dropout 0 and 0.05, node types checked);
`test_attention_two_nodes_backward_peak` (one layer, the output gradient made inside the backward:
allocated peak two <= three; one = three + N x 2048 bytes on the laptop). The other attention tests pin
`two_nodes` off where they compare three-node variants. T4 pytest of 1c66f61 (soup-c1-nodes):
**405 passed, 5 skipped, 0 failed**; Soup's 79 with apply() pass on the laptop.

# E1: the process exit and the head's bytes (branch claude/e1-exit-head-8fb01b)

## Report

**A, exit (`solution/exit_release.py`).** On the T4 our process spent 0.81-0.88 s after its threads
were gone (kernel teardown) against the base's 0.32 s: ~3.6 GB of pinned host memory handed back
page by page with nothing to overlap. `SOUP_SOLUTION_EXIT_RELEASE=1` starts a non-daemon thread at
the last step's end that frees the offload slabs (cudaFreeHost) and unregisters the weights' and
head's buffers (values stay, pageable), under the checkpoint/adapter save. `SOUP_SOLUTION_EXIT_NOGC=1`
disables the collector there (Py_FinalizeEx's 44 ms full collection is skipped). Train end -> process
end: 1.84 -> 1.27 s (-0.57) -> 1.22 s (-0.61) with NOGC (soup-e1-exit2); `=all` (also the allocator's
cached GPU blocks) another -0.035 s (soup-e1-exit3, 2 runs). No os._exit, nothing skipped.
**Recommend on: EXIT_RELEASE=all, EXIT_NOGC=1.** `solution/__init__.py`: one `if` wiring it.

**B, head (`solution/head_pack.py`, `SOUP_SOLUTION_HEAD_PACK=1`, own kernel `head_unpack_kernel`).**
Lossless 12-bit form of the bf16-origin fp16 weight: exactly 75.00 % (333.8 of 445.1 MiB), 15
escapes, every chunk verified bit for bit at build. T4: copy 1.06 -> 0.82 ms per 4,096-row chunk,
decode 0.15 ms; isolated head -9.3 ms at <= 650 tokens, +2..3 ms at >= 1,100 (hence
`SOUP_SOLUTION_HEAD_PACK_MAX_ROWS=800`). In training the head's copy wait falls 9 -> 2 ms/step, but
the power-limited T4 returns only -0.07..-0.24 s per run (per-step analysis, soup-e1-packv2/v3), and
the extra CUDA module costs +2 MiB nvidia-smi (401 -> 403). **Recommend off.**

Full run with all four on (soup-e1-full1): all 10 checks, 46.4 s / 403 MiB vs base 80.5 s.
Question for the organizers: below. Branch: `claude/e1-exit-head-8fb01b`.

## Part A: the process exit

Tool: `solution/bench_exit.py` + `solution/exit_probe.py` (`--mode bench`). Runs the harness's own
command (`harness/_train.py`, run_task's config and environment) through a wrapper script that stamps
every atexit callback, the finalization's collections and the end of the module teardown on
CLOCK_MONOTONIC, while the parent stamps Popen, each output line, and polls `/proc` (threads, state)
until wait() returns.

### Where the time goes (T4, soup-e1-exit1, 2 runs each, commit aa6d57e)

| stage (s) | base | ours |
|---|---:|---:|
| Trainer.train end -> main() end (checkpoint/adapter save, Soup's summary, harness metrics) | 0.36 | 0.47 |
| atexit callbacks (ours: weakref.finalize unregistering the registered buffers 69 ms) | 0.03 | 0.09 |
| Python finalization (its full gc: base 0.36, ours 0.05) | 0.84 | 0.13 |
| C-level exit (static destructors, CUDA runtime) | 0.83 | 0.26 |
| kernel teardown of the process (threads gone -> wait() returns) | 0.32 | **0.81** |
| train end -> process end | 2.39 | 1.75 |

Our `[solution] phase exit` mark is 0.86 s before the process end because everything after the
atexit callbacks (finalization, C exit, the kernel's teardown) comes after it; the 0.81 s kernel part
is ours: ~3.6 GB of page-locked host memory (offload slabs 2,560 MiB from cudaHostAlloc, the layers'
NF4 weights 645 MiB and the fp16 head 445 MiB registered with cudaHostRegister) handed back page by page
after the process is gone, with nothing to overlap.

### Change (SOUP_SOLUTION_EXIT_RELEASE=1, SOUP_SOLUTION_EXIT_NOGC=1; off by default)

`solution/exit_release.py`: at the last step's on_step_end a non-daemon thread synchronizes, frees
the offload slabs (`offload.release_host_memory`: cudaFreeHost through torch's host allocator) and
unregisters every registered buffer (`weight_stream.unpin_all`: the values stay as pageable memory,
so a later eval/generation is still correct, only slower), under the checkpoint save, the adapter
save and Soup's summary. EXIT_NOGC disables the collector at the same point (Py_FinalizeEx's own full
collection is then skipped; the module teardown runs as always). `solution/__init__.py`: one `if`
wiring the switch (orchestrator: please note).

Results (T4, soup-e1-exit2, commit 10e9308, ABBA 2 runs each + a warm run; seconds):

| stage | defaults | EXIT_RELEASE=1 | + EXIT_NOGC=1 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Trainer.train end -> main() end | 0.48 | 0.47 | 0.46 |
| atexit callbacks | 0.09 | 0.07 | 0.07 |
| Python finalization (of it gc) | 0.13 (0.044) | 0.12 (0.044) | 0.10 (0) |
| C-level exit | 0.26 | 0.25 | 0.26 |
| kernel teardown | 0.88 | 0.36 | 0.34 |
| **train end -> process end** | **1.84** | **1.27 (-0.57)** | **1.22 (-0.61)** |

The release thread takes 0.50-0.53 s (2,560 MiB of slabs freed, 1,090 MiB unregistered) and is done
before main() returns (the interpreter's join of it waits 0.0 ms); the main thread's own tail is not
slower (0.48 -> 0.46 s). Our kernel teardown is now at the base's (0.32 s in soup-e1-exit1). Wall in
that session: 47.7 / 48.6 / 48.5 s, i.e. inside the session's loop noise (loop 28.5-30.5 s); the
exit stages are what this switch changes and they are measured directly. What is left above the base:
~30 ms in torch.library's own finalizers (the base has the same 234-246 `_del_library` callbacks, 12 ms
there; left alone), and the post-train work (+0.1 s: the harness reads back ~41k CUDA event pairs of
our kernels' launches). `SOUP_SOLUTION_EXIT_RELEASE=all` also returns the caching allocator's free
GPU blocks on the thread (136 MiB on the T4): soup-e1-exit3 (db6a66f, 2 runs each, both with NOGC):
train end -> process end 1.116 s (=1) against 1.081 s (=all), C-level exit 0.242 -> 0.225, kernel
0.301 -> 0.278; the release thread 0.45-0.47 s either way.

## Part B: the head's bytes (SOUP_SOLUTION_HEAD_PACK=1, off by default)

Offline on the real checkpoint (233,373,696 values of the tied embedding, bf16 -> fp16):
- exponent fields 0..13; entropy 2.58 bits; ideal sign + 7 mantissa bits + H(exp) = 10.58 bits (66.1 %);
- every normal value has its 3 low fp16 mantissa bits zero (bf16 origin); all 482,053 subnormals and
  zeros fall into 4 exact shifted classes (m < 128; 128..255; 256..511 even; 512..1023 multiple of 4);
- so 17 classes in all, each an affine map `bits = sign << 15 | ADD + (M << SH)`; a 4-bit code into a
  per-chunk table of the 16 most frequent classes covers all but 15 values (exponent field 13),
  which are escapes (max 4 per 4,096-row chunk, 5 per 3,072-row chunk).
- Ratio: exactly 75.00 % (333.8 MiB instead of 445.1 MiB), chunk sizes uniform (1.5 bytes per value);
  DFloat11-style Huffman would reach ~66 % but needs a bit-serial decoder.

Format and kernel: `solution/head_pack.py`. Per chunk an A plane (sign | 7 bits, 1 byte per value) and a
B plane (two 4-bit codes per byte); `head_unpack_kernel` (own Triton kernel) decodes pairs of values:
one 16-bit load of two A bytes, one B byte, two table loads, one 32-bit store of two fp16; escapes are
patched in registers. Built once per run in a thread at peft's kbit preparation: the fp16 host copy
goes through the GPU in chunks (64K-entry bit tables for the A byte and the class), each chunk is
decoded with the training kernel and compared bit for bit with the fp16 chunk before its bytes go to
the pinned host buffer; any mismatch or overflow leaves the pack unbuilt. The head's ring then holds
packed chunks (copy stream) and each chunk is decoded into one fp16 buffer right before its GEMMs;
the packed slot is released as soon as its decode is queued. SOUP_SOLUTION_HEAD_PACK_MAX_ROWS limits
it to heads of at most that many rows (long steps are compute-bound: the decode would only add).

T4 microbench (`solution/bench_head_pack.py`, soup-e1-pack1, the real checkpoint; the head called
right after its prefetch, so nothing hides the first copies; medians of 6):

| chunk rows | copy fp16 / packed per chunk | decode per chunk | head N=300 | N=650 | N=830 | N=1100 | N=1400 | N=1970 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 1.06 / 0.82 ms (11.9 / 11.6 GB/s) | 0.14-0.16 ms | 40.2 -> 30.9 | 40.3 -> 31.1 | 40.8 -> 41.9 | 48.3 -> 50.4 | 65.2 -> 67.4 | 85.2 -> 88.1 |
| 3072 | 0.82 / 0.61 ms | 0.12-0.14 ms | 41.4 -> 29.9 | 41.8 -> 30.4 | 42.0 -> 38.6 | 50.8 -> 53.8 | 68.1 -> 71.7 | 82.1 -> 87.5 |
| 2048 | 0.55 / 0.42 ms | 0.09-0.11 ms | 40.2 -> 30.4 | 40.6 -> 34.9 | 40.8 -> 37.0 | 53.1 -> 55.8 | 65.5 -> 68.9 | 84.9 -> 87.7 |

(head ms, fp16 ring -> packed ring; every packed head bit-identical to the fp16 head.) Copy-bound
heads (up to ~800 rows) are 9-11.5 ms shorter; compute-bound heads pay the decode (38 x 0.15 ms ~
6 ms of GPU, +2..5 ms net), hence SOUP_SOLUTION_HEAD_PACK_MAX_ROWS. The decode kernel's block/warps
sweep moves it by +-10 % (1,024 pairs x 8 warps kept); it runs at ~150 GB/s read+write on the T4
(a laptop GPU with a 32 MB L2 measures it above its own D2D copy rate; a 256-entry pair table and
4-values-per-lane variants were not faster). Head memory above its start: 4,096 rows +6..7 MiB
packed (two 9 MiB packed slots + one 12 MiB decode buffer against two 12 MiB fp16 slots); 3,072 rows
packed is below the 4,096-row fp16 ring at every N (26.1 vs 28.2 MiB at N=300, 40.1 vs 44.3 at 1,400).
With MAX_ROWS the run's largest steps (which set the peak) keep the fp16 ring. Build in the thread:
0.7 s on the T4 (334 MiB pinned, 38 chunks encoded and verified), 75 MiB transient GPU memory.

In training, soup-e1-packv2 (namedesign, 59402d0, variants ABBA 2 runs each + warm, a hot session:
median step 0.43 s; pack started at peft's kbit preparation):

| variant | wall | steps 3+ | step 0 | first step mark | head copy wait/step | nvidia-smi |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| defaults | 48.31 | 28.47 | 0.565 | +16.75 s | 6.4-7.9 ms | 401 |
| HEAD_PACK=1 (all heads) | 48.32 | 28.12 (-0.35) | 0.483 | +17.11 s | 1.7-1.9 ms | 403 |
| HEAD_PACK=1, ROWS=3072 | 48.40 | 28.21 (-0.26) | 0.507 | +17.07 s | 0.7-1.0 ms | 403 |
| HEAD_PACK=1, MAX_ROWS=800 | 48.29 | 28.02 (-0.45) | 0.480 | +17.21 s | 1.8-1.9 ms | 403 |

The steps gain what the microbench says, but the build delayed the first step by 0.3-0.45 s
(setup_transformers +0.25..0.4 s: started at prepare, its cudaHostRegister of 334 MiB holds up the
setup's own CUDA calls), so the wall did not move. torch's reserved/allocated are identical (272 /
234.6 MiB); nvidia-smi +2 MiB outside the allocator (one more CUDA module). The build now starts at
the end of Soup's setup (SOUP_SOLUTION_HEAD_PACK_AT=setup, default; under the trainer build, CPU
work, where the offload prepins for the same reason): soup-e1-packv3 measures it.

Full run with the candidate switches (soup-e1-full1, peagverr, 59402d0, `--env EXIT_RELEASE=1
EXIT_NOGC=1 HEAD_PACK=1 HEAD_PACK_MAX_ROWS=800`): **all 10 checks pass**; base 80.5 s / 14,345 MiB, ours
46.4 s / 403 MiB (s 1.735 against a fast base; m 35.6), eval -0.015 %, loss curve 0.01 % / 0.05 %,
own kernels 14.0 % (head_unpack_kernel listed under check 3); 33 of 64 heads packed, the pack ready
0.2 s before train begin; the release: 2,560 MiB freed and 1,424 MiB unregistered in 0.45 s.

soup-e1-packv3 (namedesign, c0c7be2, every variant with EXIT_RELEASE=1 + EXIT_NOGC=1, ABBA 2 runs,
a cooler session): steps 3+ / wall / first step minus setup begin: no pack 25.46 / 43.62 / 5.87 s;
pack at setup end, MAX_ROWS=800: 25.94 / 44.34 / 5.87 s; pack at prepare: 26.39 / 45.60 / 6.30 s;
pack for every head: 26.20 / 44.70 / 5.88 s, and one of its two runs crossed a 20 MiB page (423 MiB,
reserved 292: the packed ring is +6 MiB at the head of the largest steps). Starting the build at the
end of the setup removes the startup cost; the step totals swing with the session's drift (the first
positions are faster) more than the pack moves them. Normalizing by the unpacked large steps of the
same runs (packed only for steps of <= 800 tokens: 31 of 64), the packed steps are 0.6 % (packv2) and
2.2 % (packv3) shorter: -0.07..-0.24 s per run. The head's copy wait itself falls from 6.4-9.7 to
1.7-2.5 ms per step (-0.45 s per run); the T4 at its 70 W limit spends the idle it loses on lower
clocks (RESEARCH: removed GPU idle never returns to the wall in full). Verdict: works, bit-exact,
ready behind its switch; not worth +2 MiB at the measured gain.

## Question for the organizers (exact wording)

> Замороженный общий вес `embed_tokens`/`lm_head` мы, по вашему разрешению, держим в pinned-памяти
> хоста и стримим чанками на GPU каждый шаг. Можно ли держать на хосте этот вес в сжатом без потерь
> виде (12 бит на значение вместо 16: байт «знак + 7 бит мантиссы» и 4-битный код класса порядка по
> таблице чанка, плюс список из 15 исключений) и распаковывать каждый чанк на GPU своим Triton-ядром
> обратно в fp16 прямо перед GEMM? Значения и dtype, подаваемые в операции, бит-в-бит те же, что у
> базы (fp16-вес): при загрузке каждый чанк распаковывается тем же ядром и сравнивается с fp16-чанком,
> при любом расхождении сжатие выключается. Сжатый вид строится заново в каждом запуске из чекпойнта
> (между запусками ничего не кэшируется), его построение и распаковка входят в замер.

English: The frozen tied embed_tokens/lm_head weight is, as you allowed, kept in pinned host memory
and streamed to the GPU in chunks every step. May we keep it on the host in a lossless compressed
form (12 bits per value instead of 16: a sign + 7 mantissa bits byte and a 4-bit exponent-class code
into a per-chunk table, plus a list of 15 exceptions) and decompress each chunk on the GPU with our
own Triton kernel back to fp16 right before the GEMMs? The values and dtypes fed to the ops are
bit-identical to the base's fp16 weight: at load time every chunk is decoded with the same kernel
and compared with the fp16 chunk, and any mismatch turns the compression off. The compressed form is
rebuilt from the checkpoint in every run (nothing is cached between runs); building and decoding it
are inside the measured time.

The exit release needs no question in our reading (no os._exit, no skipped finalization, no
background process; memory that training no longer uses is handed back on a thread while Soup
saves); if the orchestrator prefers to ask: «Можно ли после последнего шага обучения освобождать
pinned-буферы оффлоада и снимать регистрацию pinned-памяти весов в потоке, пока Soup сохраняет
адаптер (значения весов остаются в обычной памяти, все выходы пишутся как раньше), и выключать
сборщик мусора после последнего шага?»

  nvidia-smi memory.used after each step): context 107 MiB; register 334 MiB of host memory +0;
  register 1,090 MiB more +2; 10 pinned slabs of 256 MiB (cudaHostAlloc) +6; small tensors +16 (the
  first allocations and kernels of the process); load `head_unpack_kernel`'s module +0; another
  Triton module +0; unregister the 334 MiB +0. So it is the GPU-side mapping of page-locked host
  memory (about one 2 MiB step per ~1 GB pinned or registered), not the kernel module: the pack's
  334 MiB move our 645 + 445 + 2,560 MiB over the next step. Already-pinned memory with room for it is
  only the offload's spare slabs (7 of 10 used on the public data, all 10 at 2,048-token rows, where
  two slabs would be pinned again on demand, 130 ms each, and the step comes back). Verdict unchanged:
  HEAD_PACK stays off (its gain is within the session noise and the organizers' answer on the packed
  weight is pending); by the formula +2 MiB costs nothing while we have the best memory.

# L1: apply begin -> first training step (branch claude/l1-startup)

Kaggle T4 (account slerfas), one session per comparison, `--mode variants --abba --warm-run`,
means of 2 ABBA rounds; seconds from `[solution] phase apply begin` unless noted. Phases parsed
from each run's train.log (apply end, setup_transformers begin/end, train begin, first step begin,
"warmup done in", "waited ... for the warmup", "tensor loop", staging).

## Where the time went on main 8387938 (soup-l1-p0, startup sampler `SOUP_SOLUTION_STARTUP_PROFILE=1`)

- apply 3.1-3.4 s (imports 3.0 s at 96 % of a CPU), Soup CLI 0.45 s, model setup 3.3 s, trainer
  build 3.7 s, train() -> first step 0.3 s: first step at +10.9 s. The warm-up (7.2 s from apply end)
  ended 0.1-0.3 s before train begin.
- Without the warm-up (`SOUP_SOLUTION_WARMUP=0`): model setup 2.0 s instead of 3.3, trainer build
  3.5 s: the trainer build is slow by itself.
- Trainer build (3.85 s sampled): 3.34 s in datasets' fingerprint of Soup's tokenization map
  (`Hasher.hash(checked_format_row)`), of which 2.87 s is dill's pure-Python pickle of the tokenizer
  (151,643-entry `_vocab`, 151,387 `_merges` tuples: ~760 k save() calls), 0.30 s dill's `dis` text
  scan for globals, 0.41 s filelock's Python audit hook (`_audit_fork_safety`, installed at filelock's
  import; pickle calls `id()` 1.2 M times and each is a `builtins.id` audit event). The tokenizer is
  pickled exactly once per run (the second map, Soup's assistant masks, and TRL's truncation hash in
  milliseconds), so a memo of its hash saves nothing. This is what the answer-13 compliance cost
  (CHEAP_FINGERPRINT and DATASET_HASH off: trainer build 1.8 s in m6 -> 3.8-4.3 s in m7/m8).
- Model setup (3.27 s, main thread at 55 % of a CPU): tokenizer load 0.53 s, the skeleton's
  `nn.Linear.__init__` on meta 0.37 s (kaiming_uniform_ through the device context: 0.28 s), tensor
  loop 1.89 s (bitsandbytes' `get_4bit_type` per weight 0.55 s, waits for staging 0.36 s), peft 0.27 s.
  The warm-up threads spend 2.1 s of that window waiting for the C compiler (one `cc` per launcher).
- The GIL switch interval is the interpreter's 5 ms (the organizers forbade changing it): locally, on 4
  CPUs (`taskset -c 0-3`), the whole warm-up takes 3.9 s with the main thread idle, 4.0 s with it
  issuing small torch ops, 14 s with it running pure Python. Pure-Python phases of the main thread
  (dill's pickle) starve the warm-up; the warm-up's GIL handoffs slow the main thread's GIL retakes.

## Switches of this branch (all off by default)

- `SOUP_SOLUTION_LAUNCHERS_ONE` (launcher_one.py, started from warmup.py `_run`): the probe runs the
  queued registrations of the compile-only kernel modules (an explicit list) once with triton's
  `jit_cache_hook` answering "skip", their `make_launcher` sources go into one translation unit (each
  source's file-scope names renamed by `#define`, a module init that keeps each launcher's own module),
  one `cc` run, served to triton's `compile_module_from_src` by source text. Kernels (cubins) and launch
  code are triton's. Locally one launcher 0.22 s, 13 in one TU 0.34 s; whole warm-up on 4 CPUs
  3.3 -> 1.6 s. Tests launch real kernels through the combined launchers (bit-exact results), unknown
  sources and failed builds take triton's own build. T4: warm-up 6.95 -> 4.91 s (soup-l1-v2).
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_LOAD_CODE_TABLE` (existing, S1): bitsandbytes' NF4 table built once per load and cloned
  per weight. With the warm-up shorter it pays now: first step -0.27 s, wall -0.33 s (soup-l1-v2).
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_META_INIT` (load_stream.py, scoped to Soup's `_setup_transformers`): torch's init
  functions return a meta tensor untouched (the skeleton's reset_parameters on meta). Tests: generator
  states, all LoRA A/B tensors and every loaded weight bit-equal after the whole setup without
  reseeding; a real tensor gets the same values and leaves the generator in the same state.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_LOAD_EARLY` (load_early.py, started first in `startup.prepare_imports`; answer 48):
  the checkpoint's data sections read with preadv into host memory during the imports, registered with
  the driver per chunk (chunks end on tensor boundaries, read in the loader's natural key order: the
  file holds the layers alphabetically); load_pinned.py stages a tensor as a view of its chunk,
  load_stream.py's embedding cast reads from it; only for files transformers opens with the same real
  path, size and mtime; buffers dropped when the load uses none of them, after the load's final
  synchronize, and at the end of Soup's setup. Which files: the `base` of the `--config` Soup runs with
  (a hint of what to read, not a mode switch; without `--config` nothing is read), its local directory
  or HF cache snapshot. Tests: tiny load bit-equal (with and without the async embedding cast), failed
  read, other files dropped.
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_EARLY_ROWS` (existing, night): Soup's own build_format_row and `_map_text_sft_rows`
  (the same Dataset.map, datasets' own fingerprint: now checked in test_trainer_build.py) in a thread
  during the model load, so the 2.9 s of dill hashing leaves the main thread's path (answer 15).
- `SOUP_SOLUTION_TRACKER_THREAD` (tracker_async.py, hooked from startup.patch_soup_first_step_mark;
  answer 16): Soup's per-log INSERT + commit (fsync per row) by a writer thread with its own connection
  to the same database, the timestamp taken at the call, rows in call order; every other tracker use
  waits for the queue through `_get_conn`; exit waits; writer errors raised by the next call.

Deleted after the organizers' answers 8, 9 (and 13, 31): TOKENIZER_PICKLE (a byte-identical faster
pickle of the tokenizer: soup-l1-v1 first step -0.91 s, wall -0.70 s; "no" to question 8),
FAST_FINGERPRINT, DATASET_HASH with `install_fast_tokenizer_reducer`, CHEAP_FINGERPRINT,
`startup.freeze_imported_objects`, the warm-up's switch-interval code, EARLY_PROBES.

FAST_ROWS (on by default until 2a7f33e) changes datasets' fingerprint of Soup's map: on Soup's own
`_map_text_sft_rows`, the real Qwen tokenizer and 32 task rows, the rows are identical and the
fingerprint is 81be3add1e3b65ff without, d84e8ceaa6a009e2 with. dill gathers the globals to pickle
with `dill.detect.globalvars(recurse=True)`, which walks every function reachable through global names
(Soup's loss_mask helpers among them) and adds the builtins their code uses; the replacements use
`map`, `reversed`, `set`, `tuple`, `str`, `all`, `Exception`, which the originals do not. Named like the
originals: no change. As callable objects (which dill does not walk): the originals' own names
(`enumerate`, `hasattr`) disappear instead. An identical fingerprint would need the replacement to use
exactly the originals' global names. Its gain locally: 0.176 -> 0.076 s for the 256 rows.

Measured, not kept: `SOUP_SOLUTION_HELD_ENCODE` (+0.45 s), `TRITON_STORE_BINARY_ONLY=1` (-0.1 s,
within noise; it makes triton write only the cubin and the metadata JSON to the run's own cache
directory instead of every IR stage, nothing reused between runs).

## Lines for README (switches on by default)

- Лаунчеры ядер Triton собираются одним запуском компилятора C: поток прогрева один раз прогоняет
  регистрации прогрева с `knobs.runtime.jit_cache_hook` Triton, отвечающим «пропустить» (ничего не
  компилируется и не запускается, видны только сигнатуры), берёт исходники лаунчеров у `make_launcher`
  Triton и собирает их в одну единицу трансляции (имена каждого исходника переименованы через
  `#define`, каждый лаунчер сохраняет свой модуль). `compile_module_from_src` Triton получает готовый
  модуль по тексту исходника; любой другой исходник и неудачная сборка идут обычным путём Triton.
  Кубины и код запуска те же. На T4 прогрев 7,0–7,4 → 4,8–5,0 с. `SOUP_SOLUTION_LAUNCHERS_ONE=0`
  выключает.
- Таблица NF4 bitsandbytes строится один раз за загрузку и копируется для каждого веса (те же 16
  значений, свой тензор у каждого quant state); без этого `get_4bit_type` на каждый из 196 весов
  создавал её заново с ожиданием GPU. `SOUP_SOLUTION_LOAD_CODE_TABLE=0` выключает.


## П22. Заметка docs/notes/m1-modal.md

# M1: the harness on a Modal T4 (`tools/modal_run.py`)

Kaggle gives two GPU notebooks per account and a 15-25 min queue per measurement. Modal gives each
call its own container with one T4, so every session can measure at once. `tools/modal_run.py`
mirrors `tools/kaggle_run.py`: the same modes and switches, the same steps (it builds the Kaggle
notebook with kaggle_run's own `build_notebook` and runs its shell lines in order), the same output
layout and the same summary lines (kaggle_run's `summarize`).

## Switching from Kaggle

```bash
# Kaggle
wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash tools/kaggle_wsl.sh 1 --mode variants --slug soup-t15 --commit <sha> --variant a: --variant b:K=1 --repeats 2 --skip-pytest
# Modal: Git Bash on Windows with the Windows Python (3.10, modal 1.4.1 installed); no WSL
python tools/modal_run.py --profile acc3 --mode variants --slug soup-t15 --commit <sha> --variant a: --variant b:K=1 --repeats 2 --skip-pytest
```

Results go to `runs_modal/<stamp>-<mode>-<slug>/output/` (gitignored by `runs_*/`): `repo/runs*/...`
as on Kaggle (`train.log`, `metrics.json`, `result.json`, `checks.json`, `trainer_state.json`,
`eval_*.log`, `warmup.log`, plus `adapter_config.json` and `adapter_model.safetensors`), the step
log in `output/<slug>.log`, and `output/modal_status.json` (exit code and seconds of each step,
container time, PCIe width). `spec.json` and `call_id.txt` sit next to `output/`.

Every flag of kaggle_run works the same: `--mode full|solution|variants|jury|bench|diag|profile`,
`--commit <sha>|HEAD` (pushed: the container clones the team repo; the tool warns when no remote
branch has it), `--env K=V`, `--variant`, `--repeats`, `--abba`, `--warm-run`, `--jury-seed`,
`--jury-data=...`, `--bench`, `--skip-pytest`, `--no-wait`, `--attach` (with `--slug` and `--mode`:
waits for the latest run of that name and fetches it). Not needed here: `--user`, `--setup-secrets`,
`--public`, `--poll`. New: `--profile`, `--host x16|any`, `--wave`, `--waves`, `--start-timeout`, `--cpu` (default 4,
Kaggle's T4 x2 has 4 vCPUs), `--memory` (MiB, default 16384), `--timeout` (container seconds,
default 5400), `--no-prewarm`, `--github-token-file`.

Runs are detached: if the terminal or the Claude session dies, the container keeps going until it
ends; fetch it with `--attach`. To stop one: `MODAL_PROFILE=<p> python -m modal app list`, then
`python -m modal app stop <app id>`. The app is named `soup-<mode>-<slug>`. On this laptop set
`PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8` for `python -m modal ...` (the console is cp1251); the tool reconfigures
its own stdout.

## Pick an x16 host (the default)

Most Modal T4s sit on a PCIe **x8** link: 5.8 GB/s host to GPU with pinned memory, against
11.5-12.3 GB/s on Kaggle and on Modal's x16 hosts (probe of 10 containers: 9 x8, 1 x16; the host
search below saw about 1 in 6 x16). Our solution streams NF4 weights and the head over PCIe, so on
x8 its step is 0.56 s instead of 0.43 and the head waits 49 ms per step instead of 5.6: x8 numbers
do not transfer to Kaggle, and they rank PCIe-heavy variants wrongly.

So by default (`--host x16`) the tool starts `--wave` (5) containers at once; each reads
`pcie.link.width.current` from nvidia-smi before doing anything, an x8 one returns in seconds, the
first x16 one claims the run in the Modal Dict `soup-host-claims` and runs it, and the rest are
cancelled. The x16 hosts also have Kaggle's CPU clock (2.0 GHz, 14 CPUs visible, 110 GB). After
`--waves` (6) waves without an x16 host it runs on any host and says so in a WARNING line. In
practice: found in wave 1 or 2, under 2 minutes, about $0.01-0.02 of losing containers.
`--host any` takes the first container (correctness checks, quick smoke runs).

## Profiles (accounts)

`--profile <name>`, else `MODAL_PROFILE`, else the tool's default **acc6** (workspace
enotrocket2009, about $15 left per the team lead). The active profile of `~/.modal.toml` (`acc4`)
is paused, so the tool never falls back to it. All 15 profiles (`python -m modal profile list`
gives the workspace; a T4 function per workspace at 09:20 and again at 10:30; October spend from
`python -m modal billing report --for "this month" --json`, sum of `Cost`):

| profile | workspace | T4 on 31 Oct | spent in October |
|---|---|---|---|
| acc6 (default) | enotrocket2009 | ok | $44.76 |
| glofcast-prod | abzalabdrash-bs | ok | $0.02 |
| acc3 | aldiarzanybek055 | ok | $8.57 (+ about $1 of M1 runs) |
| tripleacodex | tripleacodex | ok | $12.99 |
| abdrashabzal-bs | abdrashabzal-bs | ok | $19.94 |
| acc7 | abdygalimova-sh | ok | $32.61 |
| sholpanabd79 | sholpanabd79 | ok | $42.47 |
| acc4 | abdrashabzal2009 | workspace paused | $0.00 |
| acc8 | abdrnurlan | workspace paused | $0.00 |
| acc5 | abdrash-a2009 | spend limit exceeded | $31.12 |
| acc9 | abdygalimov1974 | spend limit exceeded | $31.19 |
| acc10, acc11 | abdr-n2006 (one workspace) | spend limit exceeded | $30.19 |
| acc12, nurlan-abdr2006 | nurlan-abdr2006 (one workspace) | spend limit exceeded | $30.44 |

acc5, acc9, acc10/11 and acc12 each spent their $30 of October credit, so they are blocked until
the monthly credit renews (1 November) or a payment method raises the limit; acc4 and acc8 need
their workspace un-paused in the dashboard. The CLI shows spend, not the credit left.

When a workspace refuses the run the tool prints one line, `modal_run: ERROR: profile <p>, start:
the workspace is over its spend limit ...` (or paused, or token refused/unknown profile), and exits
with code 2 at once. Modal does not refuse a call over the workspace's GPU limit, it queues it: when
no container of the run gets a T4 within `--start-timeout` (300 s) the tool cancels its calls and
exits with code 4. A run that dies inside Modal (container stopped, credit ran out mid-run) exits 3
without outputs; a run whose steps raised exits 1 with what there is; a complete run exits 0
(whatever the checks say, as kaggle_run). All tested on 31 Oct (acc9, acc4, an unknown profile,
`--start-timeout 1`).

The image (built once per workspace, ~5 min, cached by Modal) and the
Volume `soup-hf-cache` (model and dataset as one 3 GB tar, filled by the first run of a workspace,
75 s) are ready on acc3, tripleacodex, acc6 and glofcast-prod (image only); the other workspaces
pay both on their first run. Suggested: one profile per session, so a session that burns its
workspace's credit does not stop the others.

## Cost and concurrency

T4 $0.59/h, CPU $0.047 per core-hour, memory $0.008 per GiB-hour: about $0.85/h with the defaults.
The tool prints an estimate per run. Measured: full mode 460-550 s of container time, $0.12-0.14
(with `pytest solution`, 225 s of it); variants with two runs and `--skip-pytest` 260-300 s, $0.06-0.07;
diag 137 s.

Each call is its own ephemeral app and container: no slot files, no queue on our side. Modal
limits the GPUs running at once per workspace (the plan's limit; we have not hit it with 6
containers on one workspace); beyond it calls wait in Modal's queue. A host search uses 5
containers for a few seconds each.

## What differs from Kaggle

- **A/B comparisons stay within one container**: `--mode variants` (with `--abba`, `--repeats`,
  `--warm-run`). Never compare numbers of two Modal calls, or a Modal run with a Kaggle run: hosts
  differ in PCIe, CPU and GPU clocks, like Kaggle sessions do.
- PCIe: see above; with `--host any` most runs land on x8.
- GPU: the same Tesla T4 (70 W cap, 1590 MHz max SM clock), driver 610.57 (Kaggle 580.178), one
  GPU visible (Kaggle has two; the harness hides the second one). Under a matmul load the clock
  falls to 700-1300 MHz at the 70 W cap, as on Kaggle. The base Soup run, GPU-bound, comes out
  faster than on Kaggle (79.7 s on x16, 69 s on x8 hosts, against 83.9-92.3 on Kaggle), so `s` of a
  Modal full run is not the jury's `s`.
- Check 9 holds: nvidia-smi is there and polled the same way, idle start (3-6 MiB), peaks agree,
  the allocator env is the harness's.
- CPU: gVisor hides the model. x16 hosts: 2.0 GHz; x8 hosts: 3.1 GHz; `nproc` and
  `OMP_NUM_THREADS` follow `--cpu`. Each run log starts with nproc, MHz and a single-thread loop
  timing (`python loop of 1e7 additions`, 1.3-1.5 s) so hosts can be compared.
- Software: Python 3.13.3 (Kaggle 3.13.15), torch 2.11.0+cu128, triton 3.6.0, torchvision 0.26.0,
  torchao 0.10.0 and every dependency at Kaggle's version: `tools/kaggle_freeze.txt` is Kaggle's
  `pip freeze` (taken with `kaggle_run.py --mode bench --bench "pip freeze"`) and goes to pip as
  constraints (without it pip took datasets 5.1.0 and numpy 2.5 instead of 4.8.5 and 2.1.3). Kaggle
  has ~900 more packages (sklearn, scipy, wandb, ...); the solution's diag line shows only
  torchvision of those gets loaded on Kaggle, and it is installed here too.
- Disk: the image's files load lazily on first read, so the tool reads site-packages once before
  the steps (11 s; Kaggle's pip cell leaves them warm); `--no-prewarm` turns that off. The model is
  unpacked to local disk from the Volume (7 s) before the steps; on Kaggle the harness's warm-up
  downloads it, also before the measured runs. Kaggle's first measured run pays a cold disk cache
  (~8 s); here the first run of a container still pays about 1.3 s more than the second
  (first step and start), so use `--warm-run` for variants as on Kaggle.

## План S1: холодные ядра torch на шаге 0 (п. 5)

Что известно. CUDA 12.2+ на Linux грузит модули лениво, при первом запуске ядра, и документация прямо предупреждает, что эта загрузка попадает в измеряемое окно (ссылка в таблице). Контекст создаёт харнесс до `apply()` (`harness/_train.py:120`), поэтому `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER` из нашего кода не сработает; остаётся прогрев. `warmup.py` греет наши ядра Triton, cuBLAS (`:222`) и хвост шага (`:240`: AdamW, clip, GradScaler, isnan/isinf). Ядра torch, которые идут только внутри forward и backward, не греются.

Как мерил локально. `docs/notes/r3-bench/cold_ops.py` в новом процессе вызывает каждую группу дважды с синхронизацией и печатает время первого и второго вызова:

```bash
MSYS_NO_PATHCONV=1 wsl -d Ubuntu -- bash -lc 'source ~/soupenv/bin/activate && cd /tmp && python -I "/mnt/c/Users/User/Desktop/децентратон/soup/.claude/worktrees/r3-methods/docs/notes/r3-bench/cold_ops.py"'
```

Результат (мс, первый / второй): efficient attention fwd+bwd 7,8 / 1,8; каст half в float + add_ + mul 40,6 / 0,6; isfinite + where 50,4 / 0,5; index_select 110,3 / 0,3; nonzero + cumsum 49,5 / 0,6; sum + amax fp32 56,0 / 0,2; repeat_interleave 0,4 / 0,1; strided copy_ 0,2 / 0,15. Дорогие первые вызовы приходятся на семейства ядер из ещё не загруженных модулей libtorch_cuda; копии и attention, видимо, уже были загружены предыдущими вызовами (порядок в скрипте важен). Это не список для T4, а доказательство масштаба.

Как получить точный список на T4 (первый шаг подчата, 15 минут прогона). Трасса диагностики умеет любые шаги: `SOUP_SOLUTION_DIAG_TRACE_STEPS` (`solution/diag.py:32`, старт на `step == TRACE_STEPS[0]`, `:157`). Прогон `--mode diag --env SOUP_SOLUTION_DIAG=1 SOUP_SOLUTION_DIAG_TRACE_STEPS=0,1`; в трассе для каждого имени ядра взять первое и второе событие `cudaLaunchKernel` (категория `cuda_runtime`, связь с ядром по `args.correlation`). Холодные: первый запуск дольше 2 мс при втором меньше 0,1 мс. Для справки, в прогретых шагах 8–9 той же трассы медиана `cudaLaunchKernel` 10,7 мкс. Разных ядер в шагах 8–9 всего 86 (трасса b1-diag2); из них torch-ядра (не Triton, не cuBLAS, не fmha): `fused_dropout_kernel<Half>`, `direct_copy_kernel_cuda` (strided и unrolled), `float16_copy_kernel_cuda`, `FillFunctor<uint8>`, `FillFunctor<float>`, `reduce_kernel` для Half, long, float (sum, mean, norm), `index_elementwise_kernel` (index, index_put, index_copy), `vectorized_gather_kernel`, `CatArrayBatchedCopy`, `radixSortKVInPlace`, бинарные mul/div/add float, `AUnaryFunctor` (ne, mul), `multi_tensor_apply_kernel` (уже греется step_ops), `splitKreduce_kernel` cuBLASLt (уже греется cuBLAS) и два ядра mem-eff attention.

Реализация. В `warmup.py` новая задача `torch_ops` сразу после `cublas` и `step_ops` (их порядок закреплён в 0c04921). Внутри: константные тензоры тех же dtype, что в шаге (half для активаций, fp32 для градиентов LoRA, int32 для `cu_seqlens`, int64 для индексов), и по одному вызову: `unpad.varlen_forward` и `_efficient_backward` на N = 64 с двумя последовательностями (тот же путь, что `unpad.py:213-221` и `:268-282`, включая `_expand_heads`, `.sum(3)` по группам); `torch.native_dropout(x.expand(2, n, d), 0.05, True)` с `torch.cuda.manual_seed` **не трогать**: вызывать внутри `torch.random.fork_rng(devices=[dev])` или с сохранением и восстановлением состояния, как `fused_proj.py:999-1004`, иначе прогрев сдвинет глобальный RNG и маски dropout (это ловил Codex в 49c639b); `index_select`, `index_put_`, `index_copy_`, `gather`, `nonzero`, `cumsum`, `torch.cat`, `sort` int64 (radixSort), `x.float()`, `x.half()`, `torch.where(torch.isfinite(...))`, `mean`, `linalg.vector_norm`. Список дополнять по трассе шагов 0–1.

Тест в `test_warmup.py`: (а) после прогрева в новом процессе первый шаг маленькой модели не даёт `cudaLaunchKernel` дольше 2 мс (профилировщик) или, проще, второй прогон задачи `torch_ops` укладывается в 5 мс; (б) состояние CUDA RNG до и после задачи совпадает (`torch.cuda.get_rng_state()` побитово); (в) задача не падает под `torch.set_default_dtype(torch.float16)`. Замер: ABBA в одной сессии, `SOUP_SOLUTION_WARMUP_SKIP=torch_ops` против умолчания; смотреть `step_s[0]`, `step_s[1]` и `first step begin`, а также не удлинился ли сам прогрев так, что `train begin` ждёт его (строка «waited» в логе).

## План S1: хвост сохранения (п. 3)

Последовательность после последнего шага (харнесс ставит `last_step_end` в `Probe.on_step_end`, `harness/_train.py:151-156`, всё ниже идёт после него и входит в стену):

1. `Trainer._maybe_log_save_evaluate` видит `should_save` (DefaultFlowCallback на последнем шаге) и зовёт `Trainer._save_checkpoint` (`transformers/trainer.py:3090`):
   - `save_model(output_dir, _internal_call=True)` (`:3104`), внутри `_save` (`:3871-3900`): `model.save_pretrained` (peft, `peft/peft_model.py:225`: model card `:326` и `:1686`, `get_peft_model_state_dict` `:331`, `safe_save_file` `:378`, `peft_config.save_pretrained` `:432`), затем `processing_class.save_pretrained` (`trainer.py:3889-3890`, **токенизатор №1**), затем `torch.save(self.args, training_args.bin)` (`:3900`, №1);
   - `_save_optimizer_and_scheduler` (`:3248`, `torch.save(optimizer.state_dict())` `:3299`), `_save_scaler` (`:3314`), `_save_rng_state` (`:3197`), `trainer_state.json` (`:3144`).
2. `Trainer.train` возвращается в Soup. `_assert_finite_training_state` (`soup_cli/trainer/sft.py:2532`, тело `:67-110`: `torch.isfinite(p).all().item()` по 112 параметрам LoRA).
3. `self.trainer.save_model(self._output_dir)` (`sft.py:2537`): снова адаптер, model card, `adapter_config.json`, **токенизатор №2**, `training_args.bin` №2.
4. `self.tokenizer.save_pretrained(self._output_dir)` (`sft.py:2577`): **токенизатор №3**, в ту же папку, что №2.
5. Soup: `write_run_provenance`, `tracker.finish_run`, панель rich (`soup_cli/commands/train.py:2054-2120`).

Что убрать. №3 пишет в ту же папку те же байты, что №2, его можно пропустить, только если файлы уже на месте и совпадают с тем, что было бы записано. №2 повторяет №1 в другую папку: копия файлов. Адаптер №2 повторяет адаптер №1: веса не менялись после последнего шага, тот же state dict, safetensors пишет заголовок с отсортированными ключами, поэтому байты должны совпасть; это надо проверить тестом, а не предполагать. Optimizer.pt пишется один раз, его не трогать (локально `torch.save` состояния такого размера с GPU 54 мс).

Реализация. `solution/save_tail.py`, `SOUP_SOLUTION_SAVE_ONCE=1`, только в процессе `soup train` (как `PIN_EARLY`: `sys.argv[:2] == ['soup', 'train']`). Патч уровня класса `PreTrainedTokenizerBase.save_pretrained`: первый вызов идёт оригиналом; запоминаются объект (weakref), возвращённый кортеж путей, список записанных файлов и их байты (4,6 МБ, держать в памяти до выхода; или путь и sha256) и отпечаток состояния токенизатора (`len(tokenizer)`, `tokenizer.init_kwargs`, `chat_template`, `added_tokens_decoder`); повторный вызов с тем же объектом и тем же отпечатком пишет сохранённые байты в новую папку (или ничего, если там уже лежат те же байты) и возвращает кортеж тех же имён в новой папке; любое отличие идёт оригиналом. Аналогично, но осторожнее, `PeftModel.save_pretrained`: кэш байтов `adapter_model.safetensors`, `adapter_config.json`, `README.md` по ключу «тот же модуль, версии параметров LoRA не менялись» (`p._version` у всех обучаемых параметров равен запомненному); иначе оригинал.

Побитовое равенство. Сравнивать байт в байт каждый файл в `checkpoint-64/` и в итоговой папке между прогоном с патчем и без: `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`, `chat_template.jinja` (локально два сохранения уже совпали), `adapter_model.safetensors`, `adapter_config.json`, `README.md`, `training_args.bin`. Если `README.md` или `training_args.bin` отличаются между №1 и №2 и без патча (метки времени, путь `output_dir` в args), их не кэшировать. Харнесс читает только `checkpoint-*/trainer_state.json`, заголовок `adapter_model.safetensors`, `adapter_config.json`, `rewind.jsonl` (`harness/run_task.py:62-93`), но выходы Soup должны оставаться как у базы целиком.

Тест: крошечный Qwen2 с LoRA, `Trainer` на 2 шага с `save_steps` на последнем шаге, сравнение всех файлов обеих папок с прогоном без патча; токенизатор с добавленным между вызовами токеном идёт оригиналом. Замер: строка `Trainer._save_checkpoint` в `SOUP_SOLUTION_BOUNDARY_TIMING=1` (обёртка уже есть, `step_pipeline.py:404`) и разница `phase train end` до `phase exit`; ожидание от −0,15 до −0,3 с.

## Серая зона: трекер Soup (п. 4)

Факт: `ExperimentTracker.log_metrics` делает INSERT и `conn.commit()` на каждом логе (`soup_cli/experiment/tracker.py:400-410`), база в режиме WAL (`:165`) с `synchronous=FULL` по умолчанию SQLite (проверено: `PRAGMA synchronous` возвращает 2), то есть fsync файла WAL на каждый коммит. B1 намерил на Kaggle 3,3–3,6 мс на вызов, 63 вызова на прогон, всё на границе шага при простаивающем GPU: −0,2 с, если увести в поток. Харнесс `experiments.db` не читает. Сами не делаем.

Вопрос организаторам (текст):

> Soup на каждом шаге пишет строку метрик в SQLite (`ExperimentTracker.log_metrics`: INSERT и commit с fsync, ~3,5 мс на Kaggle, пока GPU простаивает). Можно ли выполнять эти записи в отдельном потоке того же процесса `soup train` (не процессе) со своим соединением к той же базе: те же строки, те же значения, та же метка времени (берётся в момент вызова), тот же порядок, а перед `finish_run`, любым чтением трекера и выходом поток дожидается всех записей? Режим журнала и `synchronous` не меняются.

Если разрешат: `solution/tracker_async.py`, `SOUP_SOLUTION_TRACKER_THREAD=1`; обёртка `log_metrics` считает `datetime.now().isoformat()` на главном потоке, кладёт кортеж в очередь; поток не daemon, своё `sqlite3.connect(db_path)` (соединения Python по умолчанию `check_same_thread=True`), INSERT и commit; `finish_run`, `fail_run`, `get_metrics`, `get_run` и atexit ждут очередь; исключение писателя поднимается в следующем вызове. Метку времени придётся передавать в INSERT явно, то есть повторить текст запроса Soup (`:402-409`), что надо держать в синхроне с версией Soup.

## Клей GPU для C1 (п. 8)

Трасса b1-diag2 (5f2f302, шаги 8–9 под профилировщиком; профилировщик удлиняет шаг, абсолютные мс завышены), атрибуция по цепочке вызовов CPU-операций до запуска ядра:

| Ядро | мс/шаг | Где возникает | Как убрать | Побитово? |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `fused_dropout_kernel<Half>` в backward | 2,48 | `fused_proj.py:999-1004`: `_QKVRope` backward восстанавливает RNG и заново зовёт `torch.native_dropout(x16.expand(2, n, d))`, чтобы получить `dropped` для `grad_a` (`:1005`) и маску для градиента по x | (а) сохранить маску битами в forward (1 бит на элемент, 2·N·1536/8 = 384 Б на токен на слой: 0,3 MiB при 830, 0,55 MiB при 1 427; за 28 слоёв до 15 MiB живой памяти в пике, против правила «память важнее»: не советую); (б) своё ядро Triton, которое повторяет Philox torch и сразу пишет `dropped` без маски, а градиент по x маскирует в том же проходе, что и `g_drop` | (а) да; (б) только при точном повторении схемы torch: `curand_init(seed, idx, offset)` по номеру потока, развёртка по 4, размер сетки от числа SM. Высокий риск, 6–8 ч |
| `fused_dropout_kernel<Half>` в forward | 2,35 | `fused_proj.py:903-906` | убрать нельзя: маска должна совпадать с базой; можно не писать маску (`native_dropout(..., train=True)` всегда пишет bool-маску), только своим Philox-ядром, как (б) выше | только при точном Philox |
| strided `copy_` (развёртка k/v в 12 голов) | 1,28 forward + 1,35 backward + 1,40 в пересчёте (внутри `AddRMSNormBackward`) + 0,27 | `unpad.py:197-202` `_expand_heads`: `unsqueeze(3).expand(...).reshape(...)` копирует, вызовы `unpad.py:219`, `:262`, `fused_proj.py:1127` | (а) развернуть k/v один раз в пересчёте и отдать тот же тензор и forward пересчёта, и backward (сейчас развёртка дважды: `varlen_forward` в пересчёте и `_efficient_backward`): −1,3 мс; (б) писать k и v сразу в развёрнутом виде из ядра RoPE (`rope.py`, k уже проходит через него, v нет): копия исчезает, ядро пишет в 6 раз больше k, но одно чтение | (а) да, те же байты; (б) да, значения те же |
| `reduce_kernel<Half>` sum по группам | 1,53 | `unpad.py:265-266`: `grad_k.unflatten(...).sum(3)`, то же для v | слить сумму в ядро RoPE backward (оно читает grad_k), v отдельным маленьким ядром | только если повторить порядок сложения torch в fp32 для 6 слагаемых, иначе разница в последнем бите в редких случаях; проверить на реальных градиентах |
| `FillFunctor<uint8>` (обнуление) | 1,79 | внутри `aten::_efficient_attention_backward`, `zero_` рабочей области при числе сплитов > 1 (RESEARCH: `attention_backward.cu:868-895`) | `SOUP_SOLUTION_ATTN_SPLITS_KEY=1` (`unpad.py:275-281`): обнуления нет, dQ детерминирован; на T4 по стене в шуме (ночь, ABBA) | dQ меняется (сейчас он и так недетерминирован из-за атомиков) |
| `float16_copy` (fp32 в fp16) | 1,06 + 0,93 | `fused_proj.py:885` (`x16.to(half)` в `_QKVRope`) и `:1514-1520` (`_padded_half` на входе `_MLP`): выход нормы fp32 кастуется в half | норма пишет half сразу вторым выходом (`rmsnorm.py`), каст в регистре с тем же округлением к ближайшему чётному | да; RESEARCH отклонил за прогрев нового варианта ядра (от −0,15 до −0,19 с минус компиляция). С `LAUNCHER_OPT=0` и прогревом в потоке цена компиляции ниже, чем при ночной оценке: перемерить |

Итого по трассе 13,1 мс/шаг GPU, из них побитово и без новой памяти убираемы 4–7 мс/шаг (развёртка один раз, каст в норме, сумма в RoPE). При лимите 70 Вт memory-bound время возвращается в стену не целиком (E1: снятые 7 мс ожиданий головы дали от −0,07 до −0,24 с), реально от −0,1 до −0,3 с за прогон.

## Проверено и отвергнуто

- Обход `JITFunction.run` (R1 №9, «cached runner» Triton): харнесс считает и таймит наши ядра именно там (`harness/_train.py:56-76`). Мимо него ядра пропадают из `triton_launches` и `own_kernel_ms`: удар по проверкам 3 и 4, и это выглядит как обход замера. Не делать.
- fused и capturable AdamW: `optim` сравнивается проверкой 5 (`harness/_train.py:29-34`), у fused другая арифметика (RESEARCH); документация PyTorch равенства с foreach не обещает (https://pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.optim.AdamW.html).
- `PRAGMA synchronous=NORMAL` для трекера: меняет гарантии записи Soup. Поток (п. 4) даёт то же без смены семантики.
- `CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=EAGER`: контекст создан харнессом до `apply()`; жадная загрузка всей libtorch_cuda стоила бы секунды.
- Частоты и лимит мощности (`nvidia-smi -ac/-pl`): системная настройка, в контейнере без прав, меняет среду замера.
- `torch.bmm/mm/addmm(out_dtype=float32)`: [V] доступны в torch 2.11 (микропроверка), голова уже использует `addmm(..., out_dtype=float32)` (T14); fp32-выход матмула только добавляет трафик (Астра 2, раздел 4.2).
- SwiGLU в эпилоге GEMM, bias через эпилог cuBLASLt, раскладки операндов: эпилог требует своего GEMM (Triton 3.6 на sm_75 без тензорных ядер); Lt и раскладки измерены T19b в шуме (до 4 мс/шаг).
- `_assert_finite_training_state` Soup (`sft.py:67-110`): [I] 5–10 мс за прогон, не стоит патча.
- Перестановка ядер ради частоты при 70 Вт: частота T4 пересчитывается окнами 20/80 мс (RESEARCH), Астра ставит 0. Литература даёт только общее правило: compute-bound ядра идут на частоте SM, memory-bound от неё почти не зависят (https://ar5iv.arxiv.org/html/2510.06902, https://arxiv.org/html/2505.21758v2). На горячей карте помогает снижение энергии в GEMM, то есть int8 (п. 6).
- GQA через шаг 0 по оси голов без копии: соответствие «голова h читает kv-голову h // 6» не выражается одним шагом; два вызова attention на слой дают два выхода, которые пришлось бы склеивать (та же копия). Взамен п. 8, развёртка один раз.
- Щель Soup 0,55 с перед загрузкой: в ней 4–5 коммитов трекера (`commands/train.py:1832-1844`), около 15 мс; остальное импорты Soup и разбор конфига, это область S1.
- Устойчивость к горячей сессии: [V] на тех же строках цикл base_2 61,9 с против 55,6 у base_1, медиана шага решения 0,4333 против 0,4181 (RESEARCH). Законный рычаг тут только меньше джоулей на шаг: int8 (п. 6) и снятие лишних проходов (п. 8). Прогрев или пауза ради охлаждения карты не имеют смысла: наш старт и так ~15 с без нагрузки на GPU.
- Проверки харнесса, связанные со временем: проверка 4 (доля своих ядер не меньше 5 %) у нас 12–14 %, запас большой; если C1 сократит число наших запусков, доля падает только на время самих запусков, не на число. Проверка 9 (`peak >= 0.97 * reserved`): `EXIT_RELEASE=all` делает `empty_cache` после последнего шага и `torch_max_reserved_mib` не меняет. Поток выхода не daemon: если на машине жюри он идёт дольше хвоста главного потока (по E1 0,45–0,47 с против 0,46), интерпретатор подождёт, но не дольше, чем стоило освобождение без потока.

## Что это значит для времени (оценка)

Пункты 1–5 почти не пересекаются (выход, старт, сохранение, граница шага, шаг 0) и вместе дают [I] от −1,1 до −1,6 с к стене; из них −0,6 с измерено (п. 1), −0,5 с первого шага измерено (п. 2, на стене пока в шуме). С int8 ещё −0,55 с, с клеем от −0,1 до −0,3 с. От 41–44 с это 39–41 с; цель 36 с без своего GEMM на тензорных ядрах не видна (как у Астры 2: честный пол 35–38 с).

## Микропроверки

`docs/notes/r3-bench/cold_ops.py`: холодные ядра (числа выше), `out_dtype` у bmm/mm/addmm (все три работают), `tokenizer.save_pretrained` Qwen2.5 (91–122 мс, файлы `chat_template.jinja`, `tokenizer.json`, `tokenizer_config.json`). Отдельно в WSL: `_tokenizer.to_str()` 131 мс на 4,6 МБ, копия трёх файлов 18 мс, два сохранения побитово равны; `torch.save` состояния оптимизатора размера нашего LoRA с GPU 54 мс; пара событий харнесса 35,1 мкс на запуск, `elapsed_time` 1,0 мкс на пару; SQLite 3.46.1 в WAL: `synchronous` = 2, 64 коммита в /tmp WSL по 0,017 мс (на диске Kaggle B1 намерил 3,3 мс, там fsync настоящий).


## П24. Заметка docs/notes/s1-startup.md

# S1: apply begin -> first training step (branch claude/s1-startup-f929a7)

Numbers are Kaggle T4, one session per comparison, means of 2 ABBA rounds after a warm run, seconds
from `apply begin` unless noted.

## Where the time went (main a6c3fe3: soup-s1-diag0 startup profile, soup-s1-knobs)

- apply 3.3 s: imports 2.8-3.0 s (torch._dynamo 0.89 via bitsandbytes' torch.compile wrappers;
  transformers.masking_utils imports it anyway, so it cannot be skipped; datasets 0.85, peft 0.45,
  transformers.models 0.34 through squad), our modules and patches ~0.3 s; next to them triton's
  cache-key thread hashes libtriton.so (415 MB, ~1.4 CPU-s).
- Soup CLI 0.55 s, tokenizer 0.59 s, model load 3.5 s (tensor loop 2.25 s), trainer build 1.85 s,
  train() -> step 0.17 s, step 0 0.53 s (median step 0.40-0.44).
- Without the warm-up (SOUP_SOLUTION_WARMUP=0) the first step comes at 7.67 s against 9.39 s; the
  model load is 2.26 s instead of 3.58 s. The warm-up (5.5 s from apply end) ended just before train.
- The T4 box behaves CPU-bound (4 vCPUs): work moved into "idle" CPUs slows the main thread. Moving
  the 12 launcher builds into apply() made apply 0.64 s longer; holding the GIL in the row
  tokenization made the trainer build no faster and the warm-up 0.9 s longer. What helps is less
  CPU work in total, or less on the main thread.

## Switches (all off by default until measured)

- SOUP_SOLUTION_EMBED_ASYNC (load_stream.py, head_stream.py): the embedding's job returns its pinned
  buffer and a thread casts the slice into it (`copy_`, the kernel `.to()` runs); joined before the
  load returns. Bit-equal (tiny Qwen2 with and without the pinned copies, failing thread, real model).
- SOUP_SOLUTION_LOAD_PREAD (load_pinned.py, load_stream.py): the pinned staging reads each tensor's
  bytes with `preadv` from the file (byte ranges from the safetensors header, files recorded from
  `safe_open` in Soup's setup) instead of faulting in the mmap; the embedding fill too (32 MB chunks
  into a scratch, cast into the buffer). Locally the real load's staging 1.1-2.3 s -> 0.33 s, the
  tensor loop 1.6-3.0 s -> 0.77 s. Bit-equal (tiny and real model).
- SOUP_SOLUTION_TRITON_KEY=light (warmup.py): triton's cache key with libtriton.so named by size,
  mtime and inode instead of a sha256 of 415 MB (the harness gives every run an empty
  TRITON_CACHE_DIR; the key only names its entries); 0.20 s -> 0.002 s locally.
- SOUP_SOLUTION_ENTRY_POINTS (startup.py): `importlib.metadata.entry_points()` read once from apply
  begin (bitsandbytes, fsspec, Soup's plugins asked three times, ~65 ms each on Kaggle) and answered
  with `select()` while sys.path is unchanged (as the allowed packages_distributions cache).
- SOUP_SOLUTION_LOAD_CODE_TABLE (load_stream.py): bitsandbytes' NF4 table built once per load and
  cloned on the GPU for every weight (same values, own tensor per quant state).
- SOUP_SOLUTION_EARLY_PROBES=p2p (trainer_build.py): only accelerate's nvidia-smi check in the thread.
- Measuring only: SOUP_SOLUTION_HELD_ENCODE (trainer_build.py), SOUP_SOLUTION_LAUNCHERS_EARLY
  (warmup.py), SOUP_SOLUTION_WARMUP_START=setup (warmup.py).

runs of one variant). LOAD_PREAD alone -0.17 s, on top of etk -0.02 s (its embedding fill from the
file takes 0.74 s against 0.33 s in the thread, and the loop now waits on the warm-up, not on
staging). The code table with p2p probes: loop -0.12 s but the load waits longer for staging and
the train waits 0.25 s for the warm-up: no gain. Skipping step_ops: first step -0.06..-0.08 s,
step 0 +0.15..+0.17 s: a loss. With etk the warm-up (apply end + 5.5-5.7 s) ends together with

critical path.

launched in training (from 64 launches of head_finish_kernel and rms_norm_rows_bwd without the
add up to 10,688 of nf4_dequant_kernel), and nothing compiles outside the warm-up: there is no
unreachable specialization to drop (review 1, item 6: nothing to gain here).

Startup profile (aud runs, SOUP_SOLUTION_STARTUP_PROFILE=1): the main thread has a CPU 56 % of the
model setup (1.97 of 3.54 s) and 24 % of the row tokenization (0.40 of 1.69 s). The tokenization's
time is in one line, transformers' `_encode_plus` -> the Rust `encode_batch` (1.48 s of the 1.90 s
trainer build): each of the 512 calls releases the GIL and waits to get it back from the warm-up
workers (HELD_ENCODE's case). In the model setup bitsandbytes' `get_4bit_type` (functional.py:854-855,
the NF4 table per weight with a host wait) is 0.53 s of the main thread (LOAD_CODE_TABLE's case),
the wait for staging 0.30 s. The warm-up threads spend 3.1 of their 7.1 thread-seconds of the model
setup waiting for subprocesses: 2.2 s in the 12 launcher builds (cc -O0), the rest ptxas. With two
workers the warm-up is on the critical path, so the switches that shorten the main thread (HELD_ENCODE,
LOAD_CODE_TABLE) lost in v3-v5; with three workers it has 1.3 s of slack: soup-s1-v8 measures them on
top of three workers, and LAUNCHERS_EARLY again (apply now has idle CPUs since the light triton key).
Fixed in 2928db3: the launchers-ahead probe built nf4_dequant3's launcher while fused_proj.py (C1's
diet) registers nf4_dequant4.

### Lines for README (startup, switches on by default after this branch)

- Эмбеддинг при загрузке приводится к fp16 в pinned-буфер в отдельном потоке (`copy_` из того же
  среза safetensors, ядро приведения то же, что у `.to()`), главный поток в это время грузит слои;
  значения читаются только после join в конце загрузки. Побитово (тесты на маленькой и на реальной
  модели). `SOUP_SOLUTION_EMBED_ASYNC=0` возвращает исходный путь.
- Ключ кэша Triton называет libtriton.so размером, временем изменения и inode вместо sha256 от
  415 МБ (1,4 с CPU рядом с импортами на 4 vCPU). Кэш каждого прогона харнесс создаёт пустым,
  ключ только именует его записи; скомпилированные ядра те же. `SOUP_SOLUTION_TRITON_KEY=full`
  возвращает ключ Triton.
- `importlib.metadata.entry_points()` читается один раз за прогон и отвечает `select()` на тот же
  неизменяемый набор, пока не изменился `sys.path` (bitsandbytes, fsspec и плагины Soup спрашивали
  три раза по ~65 мс). Ничего не устанавливается во время прогона, ответы те же; аналог
  разрешённого кэша `packages_distributions()`. `SOUP_SOLUTION_ENTRY_POINTS=0` выключает.
- Эффект трёх вместе на T4: первый шаг на 0,38–0,45 с раньше от начала `apply()` (три сессии:
  soup-s1-v4, soup-s1-v5, soup-s1-v6), пик памяти тот же.
